_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 1 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 6 Data Detectives. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in order (data; asking a computer; a form; a table; sorting; across and down), in the lesson's own words and with the lesson's own numbers: six friends, apple 2, banana 3, mango 1, orange 0, and the twelve things of the sorting machine (red 2, yellow 4, green 3, orange 3; fruit 7, vegetable 5). The tablet is the kit's own figure (ART.figure 'tablet'); everything else is drawn here, because the Computing kit keeps its table, its form and its sorter inside closures a film cannot reach.
title: Data Detectives
subtitle: Grade 1 Computing
objectives: Know that computing devices can be used in different ways to answer many different types of question.
Know that computing devices can help to sort and organise data.
Know how to use computing devices to manually record data, including using a form.
Identify questions that can be answered using data tables, limited to categorical data.

beats.say: Data is facts and numbers we collect.
Today you are a data detective. You read it, and a computer sorts it.
Your name is data. Your favourite colour is data too.
How many pets you have is data. So is how tall you are.
Some children think data must be numbers. It can be words as well.
Once we have collected data, a computer can help us look at it.
A computer can answer many kinds of question. Each kind a different way.
Will it rain tomorrow? That is a question for the weather app.
Which way is the park? The map app knows the way.
How do you spell elephant? Search the web for that.
The web does not know what our class likes. Only our own table knows that.
A form is a page where we put data into a computer.
Amal says bananas. You tap Banana on the form, then press Submit.
Record what the person said. Your own favourite is not their data.
Six friends, six answers. The computer keeps every single one.
The computer puts every answer into a table for us.
Apple two. Banana three. Mango one. Orange none.
Which fruit did the most children choose? Banana, with three.
Did anyone choose orange? No. The orange row says nobody chose it.
A table only knows what is in it. Amal's favourite song is not in the table.

at.only: only knows what is in it

beats.say: Sorting means putting things into groups that belong together.
Here are twelve things, all mixed up. Sort them by colour.
Reds together, yellows together, greens, oranges. Done in a blink.
Now sort the same things by type. Fruit here, vegetables there.
There is no one right way. Computers help us sort and organise data.
A table has rows and columns. Rows go across.
Columns go down. One column holds one fact about everybody.
Want to know what Amal likes? Read along Amal's row.
Knowing which way to read is most of the job of a data detective.
Data is the facts and numbers we collect.
Ask a computer the right way, and record the answers on a form.

at.ask: Ask a computer the right way

beats.say: Read the table across a row, or down a column, and it answers you.
A computer sorts and organises data in a blink. You are a data detective.
